finding: only 10 of 38 die reads this project keeps were machine-locatable. A referee re-deriving the operator table by script would have got a quarter of it.
cause: twenty-odd measurement records, written one per wave, each nesting the die read differently: operators.<name>, die_reads[], reads[], sweep.<wrapper>.reads[]. Every table since W975 was assembled by hand from files that share no schema.

fix.shape: [{design, clauses, ok, wave, seed?, site?, LUT?, pnr_s?}]
fix.tool: tri table reads the canonical key first and guesses only for records written before the convention existed

the_tools_own_limit: SPLIT groups by design NAME across every wave, so it mixes source revisions with placements. gft_smul shows 1010 and 1111 because its clauses were repaired between the two (W983/W984); gft_dup_folded shows 1101 and 1111 because one netlist was placed four ways. Those are different kinds of disagreement and the tool cannot tell them apart -- the wave column can, and the output says so.

in_flight.status: running at the time this record was written
in_flight.why: 28609 LUT needing more than 62.9 ms/LUT; the 1800 s cap of W988 killed it. It is the one operator never read off silicon.
in_flight.note: recorded as IN FLIGHT rather than omitted, so the next wave does not rediscover the question
